subject: Fused Rust fit kernel (v3_fused_rust) -- the encode half of the Gravity PQ codec
status: VERIFIED BY CLAUDE. Benchmarked and tested independently. Not merged; opt-in only.

measured_speedup.method: Rust bench 0.2002 s against a Python v1 baseline of 1.373 s RE-MEASURED MOMENTS LATER UNDER THE SAME LOAD. Both arms contended by the live PASS3 pack.
measured_speedup.unpaired_number_not_used: 7.99x, against the 1.6 s baseline measured hours earlier under different load. Reported here only to name it and set it aside -- the paired number is the honest one.
measured_speedup.throughput: 321.8 GFLOP/s on 64.42 GFLOP of N*K*2D assignment work, against roughly 44 GFLOP/s for the torch path
measured_speedup.within_predicted_band: Yes. The survey predicted 5-8x with a 12x stretch and explicitly refused 10-30x. 6.86x lands inside it.

the_predicted_floor_was_fused_away.prediction: Both Claude and the reclamation survey expected index_add_ -- the centroid update, a full pass over v every iteration -- to become the Amdahl floor once assignment got cheap.
the_predicted_floor_was_fused_away.measured_profile: accumulate (fused assign + sum) 99.9 percent, pure centroid mean 0.0 percent, init 0.1 percent.
the_predicted_floor_was_fused_away.why: The implementation fuses assignment and accumulation into one pass: the running argmin and the centroid sum are computed together, so there is no separate centroid pass to be bounded by.
the_predicted_floor_was_fused_away.consequence: The remaining cost is irreducible assignment arithmetic -- N*K dots plus a running min -- not a distinct update phase. Further gains need a tighter microkernel or Metal, not more Lloyd fusion. This is a better outcome than the analysis predicted, and it supersedes that part of the reasoning.

safety_of_the_running_pack.requirement: PASS3 was live throughout, importing tools/condense/gravity_forge.py, with spawned workers re-importing from disk.
safety_of_the_running_pack.outcome: Untouched. The work stayed in its own worktree; the live working tree shows gravity_forge.py and glm52_pack.py clean; the pack advanced from 152 to 158 shards during the lane with 0 PACK_ERROR rows.
safety_of_the_running_pack.surface_in_gravity_forge: 24 lines -- the dispatch branch only. The kernel itself is a new crate (tools/fit_kernel_v3, 772 lines) plus a 181-line Python binding.

correctness.opt_in: FIT_KERNEL still defaults to v1_full_distance; v3_fused_rust is registered in FIT_KERNELS and never selected implicitly.
correctness.deterministic: Same input and seed produce an identical codebook.
correctness.reference_checked: The fused lean argmin matches a naive reference on small tie-free inputs.
correctness.byte_identity_with_v1: Ruled out by design, same class as the documented v1-to-v2 ULP tie divergence. v3 additionally uses a different init RNG (splitmix64 partial Fisher-Yates) rather than torch randperm, so trajectories differ deliberately.
correctness.oracle_discipline: v1 remains the quality oracle. The correctness question is whether reconstruction error is statistically indistinguishable, NOT whether bytes match.
correctness.tests_run_by_claude: cargo test -p fit_kernel_v3 --release: 7 passed. pytest test_fit_kernel_v3.py + test_glm52_pack_atomic.py: 10 passed.

what_is_not_done: Metal path -- CPU NEON only, deferred
A statistical recon-error comparison against v1 across many real tensors. Determinism and small-input reference agreement are proven; distributional quality equivalence is not yet.
Any use in a real pack. This is for Math-Frozen, which starts clean; it must never be flipped on under the sealed Math-Preserve run.
not_evidence_of: quality equivalence with v1 across the real tensor distribution, or any end-to-end pack speedup
